thread:
maria_support: FYI customer-repro ticket from earlier — ACME is still seeing 504s and very long tail latencies on hosted inference. They say it started after a high-volume batch job at 02:00 UTC.

maria_support: Pasted the user's error sample below (sanitized):

```
POST /v1/generate 504 Gateway Timeout
{"error":"request timed out waiting for server response after 30s"}
```

maria_support: They attached a small repro harness that sends concurrent short-chat requests with long prompt prefixes. They claim p95 is OK but p99/p(0.999) spikes to 20-30s.

ajay_runtime: Thanks — tagging in. Do we have matching internal alerts?

incidents-bot: ALERT: hosted.gateway.tail_latency high for service: hosted-inference-prod (alert_id: ALRT-2023-89). p99 latency > 10s for 5m.

paul_sre: I can see queue depth jump for the tenant on the batchers. Queue length metric (batcher.queue_depth) hit the hard limit. Snippet from metrics around the time: 

```
metric: batcher.queue_depth{tenant="acme",shard="eu-1"} 512
metric: batcher.in_flight_batches{shard="eu-1"} 12
metric: batcher.max_wait_ms 200
metric: worker.kv_cache_hits 0.02
```

paul_sre: The batcher backlog caused continuous-batching to accumulate many small requests while waiting for full batches, then some requests time out and get 504'd by the gateway.

lina_oncall: Can we repro quickly in staging? I have a small harness.

maria_support: Repro steps customer gave (sanitized):
1) 200 concurrent connections
2) each sends prompt length ~500 tokens (prefix-heavy)
3) arrival rate burst ~1500 req/s over 30s

ajay_runtime: Running a controlled run in staging now. Quick note: the tenant had aggressive prefix caching enabled which can inflate effective length because cache miss causes long KV assembly per request.

ajay_runtime: In staging run, I see batcher queue building and long waits. Captured logs: 

```
[2026-06-09T02:01:12Z] batcher: enqueue id=0x7a2 size=18 tokens queued=498 wait_ms=180
[2026-06-09T02:01:12Z] worker: kv-assemble tenant=acme duration=142ms
[2026-06-09T02:01:13Z] batcher: dispatch batch_id=347 size=4 latency_ms=3500
[2026-06-09T02:01:13Z] gateway: proxy 504 tenant=acme reason=client-timeout
```

ajay_runtime: Root cause seems to be combination of: high input token assembly (KV work), queue_depth cap at 512, and max_wait_ms set high (200ms) causing longer in-queue waits and longer tail when combined with cache misses.

maria_support: Customer angry, wants root cause and mitigation. They said this is impacting production storefront.

paul_sre: Mitigation plan I applied for quick relief:
- Per-tenant rate-limit burst applied (tenant policy) to smooth spikes.
- Temporarily lowered batcher.max_wait_ms from 200 -> 50 on eu-1 for tenant acme.
- Disabled aggressive prefix prefetch for that tenant (makes KV assembly cheaper).

deploy-bot: rollout request accepted. Job: rollout/batcher-config/eu-1 -> version v2026-06-09-01.

deploy-bot: rollout complete for shard eu-1 (5 instances), change_id=chg-8892.

paul_sre: After change, staging p99 went from ~12s down to ~1.2s under the same synthetic burst. Queue depth stayed <220.

maria_support: Customer confirmed some improvement in prod after we applied the tenant policy. They reported fewer 504s in the next 10m window.

ajay_runtime: Long-term fixes we should consider:
- tune batcher.queue_depth per-shard per-tenant (increase limit and add soft-fallback when in-flight KV ops are high),
- implement KV-assembly cost-aware routing: requests with expensive prefix assembly should be routed to dedicated fast-path or lower batching thresholds,
- expose per-tenant "max_input_cost" in Console so support can cap expensive workloads instead of blanket rate limiting,
- reduce max_wait_ms default for hosted to 50ms and rely on dynamic batching heuristics to avoid tailing.

lina_oncall: Follow-ups (assigned):
- ajay_runtime: run load tests across eu-1 and na-2 with prefix-heavy workload and produce dashboard graphs (due +24h).
- paul_sre: add a dashboard for per-tenant KV-assembly latency and a soft queue-depth alarm (due +48h).
- maria_support: coordinate post-mortem with ACME and draft communication (due +4h).

maria_support: Noted for postmortem: include the repro harness, metrics, config diffs, and the timeline of mitigations.

ajay_runtime: One more note — during the incident we saw a small set of older worker instances still running the legacy quantized runtime which had much slower KV path. Need to identify and rotate them out; they amplify tail latency.

paul_sre: Agreed. I'll run an inventory patch and schedule replacement on eu-1 legacy nodes.

maria_support: Thanks team. I'll update the customer and close the escalation once ACME verifies stability for 24h.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT: triage open (incident_id: INC-2026-334). Actions added to board.

maria_support: Closing notes recorded. Will attach full logs and the staging run artifacts to the incident ticket.
